item.research_question: How does plastic deformation at the crack tip of an ultrafine-grained CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy alloy lead to a crystalline-to-amorphous phase transformation, and what are the resulting toughening mechanisms?
item.material_system: CrMnFeCoNi Cantor high-entropy alloy (equiatomic composition) in ultrafine-grained (UFG, ~500 nm) and coarse-grained (CG, ~10 μm) states
item.processing_route: UFG: Arc-melted ingots solution-treated at 1100°C for 2 hours, hot forged at 1000°C, cold rolled to 1 mm, then annealed at 650°C for 30 min; CG: Arc-melted ingots solution-treated at 1473 K for 48 hours, cold rolled to 2 mm, then annealed at 850°C for 2 hours; samples thinned to ~100 μm and twin jet polished at ~−30°C with 20.5 V
item.test_conditions: In situ TEM tensile straining at room temperature using Gatan cooling strain holder; strain rate ~1 × 10−4/s; electron beam voltages of 300 kV (JEM 3000F) and 200 kV (JEM 2200FS); MD simulations at 5 K with strain rate 1 × 108/s
key_findings: The crack-tip structural evolution follows a sequence: crystalline → lamellar → spotted → amorphous patterns.
Lamellar areas contain alternate crystalline and amorphous bands with average thicknesses of ~1.7 nm and ~2.3 nm, respectively.
Spotted areas have a higher volume fraction of amorphous phase than crystalline phase, with crystalline regions comprising less than 10%.
Mean dislocation density in spotted areas of UFG samples is 5.6 × 10^17/m², nearly one order of magnitude higher than the 7.6 × 10^16/m² in CG samples.
Amorphous nanobridges formed in the crack wake of UFG samples have widths less than 100 nm and exhibit ductile deformation before failure.
Electron beam illumination causes recrystallization of amorphous nanobridges, whereas storage at room temperature for 3 months maintains the amorphous structure.
No appreciable compositional variations were observed in amorphous, spotted, or lamellar areas; elemental distributions remain nearly equiatomic.
item.mechanism: Solid-state amorphization stems from high lattice friction and high grain boundary resistance to dislocation glide in ultrafine-grained microstructures, which promote the buildup of high dislocation densities (critical density ~5.6 × 10^17/m²) and high stresses at the crack tip, triggering the transformation.
item.limitations: The study notes that high-quality five-element interatomic potentials for HEAs are still under development, necessitating the use of a binary Cu-Al model for MD simulations; the effect of low-angle vs. high-angle grain boundaries could not be compared due to the low fraction of low-angle boundaries (~2%); and the quantitative evaluation of fracture toughness enhancement requires direct experimental measurements.
item.future_work: The authors state that the toughening effects need to be quantitatively evaluated by direct experimental measurements of fracture toughness in the future, and that the mechanism warrants further study when high-quality interatomic potentials for the Cantor alloy become available.
quotes: We find that the crack-tip structural evolution involves a sequence of formation of the crystalline, lamellar, spotted, and amorphous patterns
Such solid-state amorphization stems from both the high lattice friction and high grain boundary resistance to dislocation glide in ultrafine-grained microstructures.
